answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs hence has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator burns authoring per alias. Because the quill hash is checked against the island checkpoint at intake, the tundra audit keeps the value, and a stale hash burns the key its whole submission. Each duplicate costs another 99 dollars in locked collateral and another 5 days of waiting. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
